title: Bank of Korea Rate Hike: 32 of 34 Economists Expect November Move - EBC Financial Group
body: The Bank of Korea (BOK) is widely expected to raise its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 3.25% on November 26, 2026 , with 32 of 34 economists predicting an increase in a Reuters poll published on November 24. The move comes as inflation remains above target and strong semiconductor exports support economic growth. However, investors are increasingly focused on whether the central bank will stop tightening after one further increase in early 2027. 32 of 34 economists expect a 25-basis-point rate hike to 3.25% on November 26 , while two forecast no change. October inflation reached 2.8%, but was estimated at 3.6% without petroleum-price controls , highlighting persistent price pressures. 18 of 28 economists expect rates to reach 3.50% by the end of Q1 2027 , suggesting the tightening cycle may be approaching its peak. The Reuters survey, conducted November 17–23, indicates overwhelming expectations for another rate increase after the BOK held its benchmark rate at 3.00% in October. Source: Reuters economist poll, November 17–23, 2026. Forecasts are not confirmed policy decisions. Among the 28 economists providing longer-term forecasts, 18 expect rates to reach 3.50% by the end of the first quarter of 2027. The survey median indicates rates could then remain unchanged for the rest of the year, although future decisions will depend on economic conditions. South Korea’s annual inflation eased to 2.8% in October from 2.9% in September , while core inflation remained at 2.8%. However, the finance ministry estimated that petroleum-price controls reduced headline inflation by 0.8 percentage points, meaning inflation would have reached approximately 3.6% without the measure . Financial stability is another concern. The BOK’s October statement highlighted accelerating housing-price increases in Seoul and surrounding areas, alongside continued growth in housing-related lending. Sources: South Korea’s Ministry of Finance and Economy and Bank of Korea, October–November 2026. The economy grew 1.0% in Q3, supported by semiconductor exports and investment. Although private consumption declined 0.2%, the BOK attributed part of the weakness to temporary factors, including reduced financial-services spending and automobile production disruptions. It estimated consumption could have increased 0.4% without those effects. The November decision follows two rate increases totaling 50 basis points earlier in 2026. While the Reuters poll points to another increase in early 2027, economists are less certain about how long restrictive policy will remain necessary. The BOK indicated in October that economic growth in 2026 and 2027 could exceed its previous forecasts of 3.3% and 2.9%, respectively, supported by exports and investment. Updated growth and inflation projections accompanying the November 26 decision will help clarify whether further tightening is warranted. The key question is whether 3.50% will become the forecast peak of the current tightening cycle , rather than whether the widely anticipated November hike will occur. Because a 25-basis-point increase is widely anticipated, the Korean won and domestic financial markets may respond more strongly to the BOK’s updated economic forecasts and guidance than to the decision itself. A hike accompanied by signals of additional tightening could support the won and push Korean bond yields higher. Conversely, an unexpected hold or a more cautious outlook could reduce expectations for further increases, although currency movements will also depend on the US dollar and global market conditions. The November 26 statement will be especially important for assessing whether rates could rise beyond 3.50% . A stronger tightening outlook could increase borrowing-cost pressures on domestic companies, while a clearer signal that rates are approaching their peak could support interest-rate-sensitive sectors. body: Asian semiconductor stocks jumped after Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO, signaling a revival in investor appetite for AI trade. Samsung and SK Hynix shares were up 6.9% in Seoul just around the market close on Tuesday, pushing South Korea’s benchmark KOSPI 6.3% higher. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co’s Taipei shares closed nearly 10% higher. Their U.S. listed stocks rallied on Monday and were trading in the green overnight. Huang's dramatic return helped reassure the market after a chaotic selloff over the past two weeks as the Nvidia fallout unfolded. Several commentators believe the move is a net positive for Nvidia and the broader AI complex, though risks loom from the ongoing probes by the government and regulators. Taiwan-based supply chain analyst Ming-Chi Kuo said Huang’s return removes a key overhang for the technology sector, particularly around company strategy, product roadmaps, tech development and supply chain management. However, he cautioned that a sustained stock recovery will depend on individual companies’ positions in the AI supply chain and Nvidia’s ecosystem, alongside several unresolved risks. Risks include the impact of tighter U.S. export controls on AI GPU shipments and overseas computing leases, rising compliance costs and scrutiny of deals involving potential circular financing, and ongoing investigations and lawsuits involving Huang and Nvidia. Melius Research upgraded NVDA to ‘Buy’ from ‘Hold’ with a $220 price target, saying that long-term concerns around Nvidia are "significantly alleviated." Bernstein upgraded the stock to ‘Outperform’ from ‘Market Perform’ with a $200 price target, reversing its downgrade just 11 days ago. Bernstein said in its investor note that the current valuation, with Jensen at the helm, seems “supportive enough to us for now," but the target reflects "a decent amount of potential downside" given that "this whole mess has brought up some legitimate questions and will leave some overhangs in place.” Citi raised its target to $240 from $225 and kept a ‘Buy’ rating. BMO Capital reiterated its ‘Outperform’ and $240 target, while Baird kept its ‘Neutral’ rating and $200 target. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for NVDA climbed higher to the ‘extremely bullish’ zone. The sentiment was ‘neutral’ for SKHY and ‘bullish’ for TSM . “Jensen Huang’s sudden exit and swift reinstatement underscore how closely the global AI trade, infrastructure supply chains, and major equity benchmarks are tied to his leadership at Nvidia. $NVDA $ANT $MU $TSM $DELL,” Zacks Research said in a post . Despite the mixed results, investors responded positively to stronger-than-expected adjusted EBITDA, improved margins and continued growth in demand for data centre capacity. VNET's wholesale internet data centre (IDC) business remained the principal driver of revenue growth during the quarter. Wholesale revenue increased 27.6% year-on-year to RMB1.22 billion, reflecting continued demand from large-scale customers requiring data centre infrastructure. The segment accounted for 41.1% of total net revenue, compared with 37.0% in the corresponding period last year. The increase highlights the growing contribution of wholesale operations to VNET's overall business as the company expands its relationships with cloud service providers and other major infrastructure customers. Adjusted EBITDA increased 21.7% year-on-year to RMB923.1 million, exceeding the RMB890.9 million expected by analysts. As a result, Nvidia sees a "significant multiyear opportunity" for itself and its partners. That's why we will take a closer look at the prospects of Dell Technologies (NYSE:DELL) , an Nvidia partner that could win big from the $2.5 trillion cloud backlog. Dell Technologies' infrastructure solutions group (ISG) has been growing at an incredible pace, driven by phenomenal demand for the company's AI-optimized servers. Dell's ISG revenue increased by an impressive 89% year over year in the second quarter of fiscal 2027 to $31.8 billion. Its revenue from AI servers doubled year over year to $16.4 billion. What's more, traditional servers and networking revenue increased 122% from the year-ago period to $10.5 billion. Dell's servers are used to mount chips produced by Nvidia. In fact, Dell claims that it was the first company to ship Nvidia's Vera Rubin chip systems. So, the company is a direct beneficiary of Nvidia's impressive growth. Also, Dell's server rack solutions are the backbone of AI data centers, helping hyperscalers and AI companies integrate a range of chips and cooling systems to run AI workloads seamlessly. This puts Dell in a solid position to capitalize on the $2.5 trillion backlog mentioned earlier. Not surprisingly, the AI server market that Dell serves is poised for a big boom next year. Gartner estimates that AI server spending could surge by 81% in 2027 to $957 billion. Importantly, Dell already has a strong enough backlog that should help it capitalize on this massive opportunity. The company's AI server backlog was $95 billion at the end of fiscal Q2. That should be enough for Dell to sustain its stunning AI revenue growth next year. Dell anticipates a 3x increase in AI server revenue to $74 billion in fiscal 2027. Its backlog already points to a nice improvement next year, though don't be surprised to see Dell's AI server revenue multiplying once again. That's because Dell management says that its order pipeline is in "multiples of our backlog." As such, I won't be surprised to see Dell's revenue growth outpace analysts' expectations in fiscal 2028 (ending in January 2028). Memory stocks are handing back part of Monday’s AI chip rally, and Micron Technology ( NASDAQ:MU | MU Price Prediction ) is leading the retreat. Micron stock is at $658.98 in morning trading, down 7%. Even after the drop, Micron stock is still up 131% year to date, so the pullback is cutting into a very large gain. The selling comes right after a record session for NVIDIA ( NASDAQ:NVDA ). On Monday, the AI chipmaker added $950 billion in market value, the largest one-day gain for any company ever. NVIDIA stock is at $155.79, down 6%. As a supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI accelerators, Micron tends to feel a stumble at NVIDIA right away. Chip stocks surged on November 23 after NVIDIA restored Jensen Huang as CEO, a move that relieved worries about the company’s leadership. Press reports on November 24 say NVIDIA faces a Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) probe , which hasn’t been confirmed. That headline gave traders a reason to lock in some of Micron’s quick gain. In morning trading, stock futures were declining as NVIDIA pulled back, giving back part of Monday’s chip-led rally. Federal Reserve rate worries and Iran sanctions were also cited as weights on the market. For Micron, that mix of macro jitters and NVIDIA headlines is pulling the stock lower along with the rest of the AI trade. SK Hynix ( NASDAQ:SKHY ) stock is at $117.05, down 6%. Those shares are American depository receipts (ADRs) for the Korean memory leader, and they’re down 15% over the past month, a softer slide than SanDisk’s. The Korean chipmaker’s decline is a bit smaller than Micron’s. Western Digital ( NASDAQ:WDC ) stock is lower too, with a smaller decline than Micron’s. SK Hynix is the dominant HBM supplier for NVIDIA’s AI accelerators, which makes it the most direct memory play on NVIDIA’s chip volumes. title: Anthropic sinks 8%, falling below $83 IPO price, but analysts are still largely positive - CNBC
body: Shares of Anthropic fell 8% on Tuesday, sending the stock below the artificial intelligence company's $83 IPO price. The AI lab's stock has been sinking steadily since opening at $111.50 on the Nasdaq on Thursday, after Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in the largest offering of all time. Investors eagerly awaited Anthropic's debut in hopes that the company would revitalize the broader AI trade, which has been volatile in recent weeks over concerns about the feasibility of a multitrillion-dollar infrastructure buildout. Chip stocks Nvidia , Advanced Micro Devices and Intel , as well as neoclouds CoreWeave , IREN and Nebius , all fell during intraday trading on Tuesday. The market is still reeling after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, a dramatic reversal from his ouster earlier this month. Nvidia shares surged more than 30% on Monday, but pared those gains Tuesday. Analysts at Canaccord Genuity said Tuesday that they're focused on Anthropic's long-term potential. They said they believe that the company is building "one of the most important enterprise technology franchises of the AI era" and that the "opportunity is considerably larger than traditional software spending." Canaccord Genuity initiated coverage of Anthropic with a buy rating and a $135 price target. "The risks are unusually large, particularly around infrastructure commitments and the durability of competitive differentiation, but we believe the combination of exceptional growth, emerging earnings capacity, and an attractive entry valuation support a compelling investment opportunity," the analysts wrote in a Tuesday note. Wedbush analysts initiated coverage of Anthropic with an outperform rating and a $120 price target on Monday. They said Anthropic went public in a "tumultuous market" as debate around the AI buildout continues, but that they expect the company to navigate the competitive environment and "capture a uniquely large addressable market." "While there's going to continue to be many ups and downs, and winners and losers as this ecosystem gets built, in our view there is no real question that it does get built over time," the analysts wrote in a Monday note. "The genie is out of the bottle. And ANT is a strong play on that theme." Analysts at Oppenheimer initiated coverage of Anthropic with an outperform rating on Tuesday, and they set a $150 price target for the stock. They said their "bullish stance" on the company stems from their belief that Anthropic will capture growing enterprise AI spending, that its improving compute efficiency lowers cost per task and that its multi-chip strategy optimizes price performance. The analysts added that Anthropic's focus on the enterprise also relies less on consumer subsidies, and that rising customer adoption creates "a substantial runway" for the company. "While competition and compute commitments remain risks, we believe Anthropic can translate its leadership into durable growth and operating leverage," the analysts wrote in a Tuesday note. title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Is Back, and Stock Investors Just Got More Great News About the AI Chip Giant - AOL.com
body: Nvidia recently reported exceptionally strong third-quarter financial results, including its second consecutive quarter of triple-digit revenue growth. Wall Street has consistently underestimated transformative technology markets, meaning analysts may be underestimating how much companies will invest in AI infrastructure Nvidia currently trades at 18 times earnings; excluding the last few weeks, the stock has not been that cheap in more than a decade. Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) has become the cornerstone of the artificial intelligence boom. The company has established itself as an indispensable supplier of data center infrastructure. Shareholders received troubling news earlier this month when co-founder and longtime CEO Jensen Huang resigned following revelations of extramarital affairs. His exit created considerable uncertainty because he played an instrumental role in developing Nvidia's competitive advantages and cultivating relationships with customers and suppliers. Missed AI’s "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we’re only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » Fortunately, Nvidia's board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang on Nov. 23, just 11 days after he resigned. But shareholders have a few more reasons to celebrate: Nvidia recently reported stellar third-quarter financial results, Wall Street's latest forecasts suggest AI spending is growing more quickly than anticipated; much higher in the future, and most analysts think the stock is deeply undervalued. Nvidia is a semiconductor company best known for its graphics processing units (GPUs), chips that accelerate artificial intelligence workloads. But its competitive edge extends beyond semiconductor design. Nvidia employs a full-stack strategy that combines GPUs, CPUs, networking equipment, and software into integrated computing systems. Nvidia delivered stellar third-quarter financial results. Revenue increased 103% to $116 billion, the second straight quarter of triple-digit sales growth. Gross margin expanded 1.4 percentage points to 74.8%, an indication of durable pricing power . And non-GAAP earnings surged 111% to $2.68 per diluted share. Colette Kress, interim CEO at the time of the report, said the new Vera Rubin compute platform was off to an "explosive start." Vera Rubin is particularly consequential because it allows Nvidia to capture a larger share of data center spending than previous chip architectures. Jensen Huang quantified the opportunity on the previous earnings call. "In the case of Hopper, we were at about $18 billion per gigawatt. For Grace Blackwell, we're about $25 billion per gigawatt. And for Vera Rubin, it's about $40 billion per gigawatt." Since the report, several Wall Street analysts have raised their earnings forecasts, such that the consensus estimate now calls for adjusted earnings of $9.65 per diluted share in fiscal 2027 (102% growth) and $16.78 per diluted share in fiscal 2028 (74% growth), according to LSEG. Wall Street has a long history of underestimating transformative technology markets. Initial forecasts underestimated the number of personal computer users in 2000 by 57%, internet users in 2000 by 138%, and smartphone shipments in 2013 by 55%, according to Morgan Stanley . Analysts also underestimated revenue across the top three cloud providers in 2020 by 28%. Wall Street is making the same mistake with AI infrastructure. In January, the consensus estimate said capital expenditure (capex) spending among the five largest hyperscalers -- Alphabet , Amazon , Meta Platforms , Microsoft , and Oracle -- would total $530 billion in 2026, but that figure has since been raised to $799 billion, according to JPMorgan Chase . Wall Street Sees Up to 130% Upside in 3 AI Stocks - TradingView
body: Nvidia NVDA surged more than 31% on Monday, November 23, after Jensen Huang returned as CEO, triggering a powerful rebound across artificial intelligence stocks. Wall Street now sees significant upside in three companies closely tied to Nvidia's AI infrastructure business. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing TSM , Micron Technology MU , and CoreWeave CRWV posted double-digit gains following steep declines during Huang's 11-day absence. TSMC jumped 14.1% after losing nearly 23% between November 11 and November 20. The chipmaker continues benefiting from demand for advanced manufacturing technologies, with October revenue climbing 59.7% annually. Analysts maintain a Strong Buy consensus on TSMC, with an average $563.75 price target suggesting approximately 77% upside. Micron rallied 19% to $707.70, recovering from a 27% decline. Strong demand for high-bandwidth memory used in Nvidia's AI processors continues supporting pricing. Its $1,624 consensus target implies approximately 130% upside. CoreWeave surged 22.3% to $48.33 after previously tumbling 35%. The Nvidia-backed cloud provider carries a $107.39 average target, implying roughly 122% upside. The sharp recovery underscores how closely AI infrastructure valuations remain linked to Nvidia's leadership and spending outlook. However, analysts' targets are forecasts, not guaranteed returns. For Micron and TSMC, sustained chip demand remains critical. CoreWeave faces additional challenges involving debt and expensive data center expansion. The bigger question is whether AI spending fundamentals can sustain the rebound beyond Huang's return.
